title: Saida Mirziyoyeva to Represent Uzbekistan at the 81st UN General Assembly
dek: The head of Uzbekistan's Presidential Administration is taking part in the general debate in New York and met UN Secretary-General António Guterres.

title: EU Removes Usmanov and Fridman From Sanctions List, Angering Ukraine
dek: On 22 September the EU delisted Chust-born billionaire Alisher Usmanov and Alfa Group co-founder Mikhail Fridman while rolling over measures on some 3,000 others.

title: Gaza's School Year Opens in Tents: 541,000 Students Return
dek: Per the Palestinian Ministry of Education, about 541,000 students returned to education on 19 September 2026. UNICEF says ~98% of school buildings are damaged; most learning is in tents and damaged classrooms.

title: How to read the news: media literacy basics
dek: Proven techniques for checking information — the SIFT method, lateral reading, telling news from advertising, and verifying images. A facts-only practical guide.

title: Kazakhstan to Build Its First Nuclear Plant: $16.5 Billion EPC Deal With Rosatom
dek: On 3 September 2026, Rosatom and KNPP signed an EPC contract for Kazakhstan's first nuclear plant. Two VVER-1200 units (2,400 MW) will be built on Lake Balkhash; Russia will finance ~85%.

title: Israel Has Targeted Ceasefire Negotiators: The Facts on Doha (2025) and Tehran (2024)
dek: Two documented events: a 9 September 2025 strike on Hamas's negotiating leadership in Doha (six killed, Israel claimed responsibility), and the 31 July 2024 killing of Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran. Facts only, with balance.

title: The third wave of Uzbek migration: post-Soviet labor migration (1991–2010)
dek: The economic labor migration that began after the USSR collapsed — mainly to Russia, then Kazakhstan and Korea. A neutral history with dates, estimated figures and sources.

title: Iran Sends Conditions to End Its War With the US via Qatar; Oil Tops $100
dek: Per Iran's SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei, Tehran set three conditions to end the war: a halt to fighting on all fronts, release of frozen funds, and an end to the naval blockade. Oil crossed $100/barrel on 9 September.
tags: Eron AQSh Neft Geosiyosat Yaqin Sharq

title: Uzbekistan Draws 9.1 Million Foreign Visitors in Eight Months as Tourism Exports Hit $4.6 Billion
dek: Foreign arrivals rose 21.1% to 9.1 million in January–August 2026. Tourism service exports grew 53.5% to $4.6 billion, and average spending per tourist reached $503.

title: Islam Karimov: the first president of independent Uzbekistan (1938–2016)
dek: Born in Samarkand in 1938, Islam Karimov led the state from 1991 until 2016. His biography, rule and contested events — a neutral, sourced history with dates.

title: Bank accounts and credit history in the USA: basics for newcomers
dek: Opening a bank account, the difference between an SSN and an ITIN, FICO credit scores, and building credit from scratch — a facts-only guide for immigrants in the USA.

title: Kazakhstan Offers Canada a $255 Million Export Package
dek: On 16 September 2026, the trade ministers of Kazakhstan and Canada discussed a list of potential exports across 45 product categories and a joint economic action plan in a phone call.

title: U.S.–Uzbekistan Trade Tops $1 Billion: Washington Deals and New Investment
dek: Bilateral trade reached $881 million in 2024 (+15%) and exceeded $1 billion in 2025. At the 6 November 2025 Washington meeting, deals on Boeing aircraft, critical minerals and agriculture were announced.

title: Central Asia's Regional Organizations Explained: SCO, CIS, EAEU, CSTO, ECO and OTS
dek: A facts-based reference on the main organizations the Central Asian states belong to — the SCO, CIS, Eurasian Economic Union, CSTO, ECO and the Organization of Turkic States — their founding dates, members and Uzbekistan's status.
tags: Ma'lumotnoma Markaziy Osiyo Geosiyosat Tashkilotlar O‘zbekiston

title: The Changed Aral: A Dried Sea, a Saxaul Forest, and the Aral School in Nukus
dek: The Aral Sea has lost about 90% of its size, and a new desert, the Aralkum, has formed in its place. Now a forest is being planted on the dried seabed, and ACDF has opened the Aral School residency in Nukus.

title: The First Years of Independent Uzbekistan: Building the State (1991–1994)
dek: After the 31 August 1991 declaration of independence — the 29 December referendum, state symbols, the 1992 Constitution, UN membership and the introduction of the national som. A factual history with dates and figures.

title: What Remittances Are and Why They Matter: An Explainer for Uzbekistan
dek: What a remittance is, the channels money moves through, the global scale, and the numbers for Uzbekistan (Central Bank and World Bank data) — a facts-based explainer.
tags: Ma'lumotnoma Moliya Migratsiya Pul o‘tkazmalari O‘zbekiston

title: Kyrgyzstan Is Building Its First GDP-Compliant State Pharmaceutical Warehouse
dek: On 16 September 2026, construction began in Bishkek of the country's first GDP-standard state pharmaceutical warehouse and logistics complex for Kyrgyzpharmatsiya. Total investment is 650 million som.

title: The Second Wave of the Uzbek Diaspora: World War II and Post-War Emigration (1940–1960)
dek: Wartime captivity, displaced persons, and the formation of Uzbek-Turkestani communities in the US, Turkey and Saudi Arabia — a neutral, factual history with dates and sources.

title: Central Asian States Are Expanding Domestic Drone Production
dek: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan are ramping up domestic UAV production to reduce dependence on foreign suppliers.

title: Kyrgyzstan and China Move Toward Mutual Recognition of Organic Product Certification
dek: On 17 September in Bishkek, meeting a SAMR delegation, the two countries reached a principled agreement to work toward mutual recognition of organic certification systems. The aim is to simplify Kyrgyz organic exports to China.

title: The Basics of Islamic (Halal) Finance: What Riba Is and How the System Works
dek: A facts-based explainer on the prohibition of riba (interest), the core principles and instruments of Islamic finance — murabaha, ijara, mudaraba, sukuk — its global scale, and Uzbekistan's steps in this direction.

title: Uzbekistan's Independence: The Road to 31 August 1991
dek: From the Declaration of Sovereignty (1990) to the declaration of independence on 31 August 1991 and the December referendum — a factual history with dates, figures and the first steps of nation-building.

title: The First Wave of the Uzbek Diaspora: Emigration in 1917–1934
dek: The political-refugee wave that followed the Russian Revolution, the fall of Bukhara and Khiva, the Basmachi movement and forced collectivization — a factual history of how the Uzbek and Turkestani diaspora took shape.

title: How Labor Migration Actually Works: The Rules for Russia, Korea and Europe
dek: An explainer on the three main legal routes for Uzbek labor migrants — Russia's patent system, South Korea's EPS program and organized recruitment — how each is structured, its rules and its numbers.

title: Timur Turlov Runs for FIDE President: He Outlines His Platform at the Samarkand Olympiad
dek: The 46th Chess Olympiad is under way in Samarkand, and the FIDE presidential election is set for 26 September. Timur Turlov is running on a ticket with Viswanathan Anand and has laid out a platform focused on education, technology and calendar stability.

title: Kazakh National University of Sports Joins Global Olympic Studies Network — First in Central Asia
dek: The Astana-based university has joined the IOC-coordinated academic network of Olympic studies and will set up a Center for Olympic Studies, Education and Legacy.

title: Kazakhstan Postpones New Royalty System for Solid Minerals to 2029
dek: The government moves the royalty from 1 January 2027 to 1 January 2029. Several technical questions remain unresolved.

title: Kyrgyzstan Is Cleaning Up the Soviet-Era Mailuu-Suu Uranium Legacy
dek: Central Asia's largest uranium legacy site holds about 2 million cubic metres of radioactive waste. With an EBRD grant, remediation is set to run through 2032.

title: Five Activists Sentenced in Almaty: 5 to 5.5 Years in the Alleged "Akorda Seizure" Case
dek: The Almaly district court delivered its verdict on 8 September. Prosecutors had asked for eight years each; the hearings were held behind closed doors.

title: FIDE Elects Its President in Samarkand: Three Tickets and ~200 Federation Votes
dek: The vote falls on 26 September at the FIDE General Assembly held alongside the 46th Chess Olympiad. Incumbent Arkady Dvorkovich suspended his powers in July after EU sanctions.

title: Kazakhstan Exports Billions in Gold but Records Just $7.2 Million in Jewellery Output
dek: Three destinations took roughly $2 billion of Kazakh gold in 2025. The government is tightening hallmarking and control over precious-metal turnover.

title: A $2 Billion Exploration Push in Ustyurt: bp, SOCAR and Uzbekneftegaz Prepare the First Well
dek: A managing committee meeting in Tashkent on 7 September confirmed that 3D seismic fieldwork is complete. The agreement covers six blocks in Karakalpakstan; bp holds 40%, SOCAR 30% and Uzbekneftegaz 30%.

title: Kazakhstan to Build Its First Food Cluster on the South Korean Model
dek: Shin-Line Group, Central Asia's largest ice cream maker, signed a memorandum in Seoul with the Korea Food Industry Cluster Promotion Agency. The Korean side will provide consulting and expert support on cluster management.

title: Seoul Hosts the First Central Asia–Republic of Korea Summit
dek: On September 16 President Lee Jae Myung received the leaders of all five Central Asian states. A cooperation forum that had run at ministerial level since 2007 was raised to the level of heads of state; a Seoul Declaration was set to be adopted.

title: EU–Uzbekistan: EPCA in Force Since 1 March, GSP+ Rules Change in 2027
dek: The Enhanced Partnership and Cooperation Agreement was signed on 24 October 2025 and has been provisionally applied since 1 March 2026. Requirements under the EU's preferential trade scheme tighten next year.

title: Labour Migration From Central Asia to Russia Falls 15%; Kyrgyzstan Down 16.7%
dek: Russian border-service data show work-related entries by citizens of three Central Asian states fell from 2.3 million to 1.9 million in the first half of 2026. Kyrgyzstan recorded 289,100 entries.

title: Karachaganak Halts for Maintenance: Kazakh Output to Fall by up to 450,000 Tonnes
dek: The field is under planned maintenance from 7 September to 1 October. Kazakhstan had already cut its 2026 oil plan from 98 to 96 million tonnes because of attacks on CPC infrastructure.

title: Pax Silica vs WAICO: Kazakhstan Is in Both AI Blocs, Uzbekistan Has Applied
dek: Kazakhstan joined the US-led Pax Silica initiative on 25 June and China's WAICO on 16 July. Reuters reported that Washington is preparing to ask dozens of countries to choose.

title: Why Is Uzbekistan Losing Its Women Engineers?
dek: Women engineers are leaving the profession — especially in the energy sector — under family pressure, hiring barriers and poor workplace conditions. The attrition starts at the education stage.

title: Tokayev Meets US Envoy at BRICS — Trump Sends a Personal Message
dek: On the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Kazakh President Tokayev met US Special Envoy Sergio Gor, who conveyed a personal message from President Trump.

title: China Becomes Central Asia's Top Trade Partner — Russia Left Behind
dek: In 2025, China–Central Asia trade crossed $100 billion for the first time, hitting a record $106.3 billion. China became the region's largest trade partner for the first time.

title: Uzbekistan Relists Unsold State Assets at ~$83 Opening Bids
dek: 84 state assets that found no buyer for years will be re-auctioned at a starting price of just 1 million soum (~$83). The required down payment is cut from 35% to 15%.

title: Is the Hijab Banned in Kazakhstan? The School Ban and the Secularism Debate
dek: Short answer: there is no blanket ban — but in schools the hijab is prohibited under uniform rules. That restriction has sparked fierce debate over secularism and religious freedom in Kazakhstan.

title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Sign 13 Documents in Seoul
dek: Talks between Mirziyoyev and Lee Jae-myung concluded with an exchange of cooperation documents on critical minerals, artificial intelligence and defense. The meeting came on the eve of the first Korea–Central Asia summit on Sept. 16.

title: Mahmoud Khalil Files Suit Against Columbia University, Alleging Failure to Protect Students From Doxxing
dek: The complaint was filed in federal court in Manhattan on Sept. 14. It accuses the university of failing to protect students harassed because of their Arab or Muslim background.

title: Nearly 100,000 Uzbeks Returned From Russia in 10 Days
dek: According to the Migration Agency, 96,415 citizens returned home between Aug. 25 and Sept. 5 — against the backdrop of Russia's tightening migration policy.

title: The Largest Chess Olympiad in History in Samarkand: 400 Teams, 1,980 Players
dek: The 46th Chess Olympiad will be held in Samarkand from Sept. 15 to 27. According to FIDE, the number of participating teams is 20 more than the 2024 record in Budapest. Uzbekistan's men's team starts as the third seed.

title: Houthis Seize Two More Strategic Islands in the Red Sea; Saudi Arabia Carries Out Strikes
dek: The Greater and Lesser Hanish islands have been brought under control. Roughly 12 percent of world trade passes through the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

title: Conference of Central Asian Women Journalists in Tashkent: A Regional Program Through 2029 Under Discussion
dek: The second conference, held Sept. 14–15, brought together more than 100 journalists and media managers from five countries. The main themes were digital security and deepfakes.

title: Strikes Continue in Gaza: Two Killed on Sept. 13, Hospital Generators Shut Down
dek: A vehicle was struck in the Tal al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City on Sept. 13. According to the Health Ministry, hospital generators have failed because of a fuel shortage. The total death toll has reached 73,669.

title: Indian Company Brings Gold Mine Online in Kyrgyzstan: $34.2 Million Spent on the Altyn Tor Project
dek: President Sadyr Japarov opened the processing plant in an online ceremony on Sept. 13. The project is expected to create close to 400 jobs.

title: Javokhir Sindarov Outscores Carlsen and Nepomniachtchi at the Global Chess League
dek: At the tournament held in Bengaluru from Sept. 5 to 13, the Uzbek grandmaster scored the most points on the Icon board. His team finished third overall.

title: CSTO “Rubezh-2026” Exercises Begin in Kazakhstan, With a Cross-Border Incursion as the Main Scenario
dek: From Sept. 12 to 19, rapid deployment forces are training in mountain and desert conditions at the Koktal range in the Zhetysu region.

title: BRICS Adopts New Delhi Declaration: 140 Paragraphs on UN Reform and AI Governance
dek: The 18th BRICS summit was held Sept. 12–13 under India's chairmanship. The declaration addressed tensions in the Middle East, reform of the UN Security Council, unilateral sanctions and settlements in national currencies.

title: Pezeshkian at the BRICS Summit: “Unilateral Sanctions Directly Affect Food Security”
dek: At the summit in New Delhi, Iran's president called for expanding trade in national currencies and said international mechanisms need reform.

title: Tokayev Meets U.S. Special Envoy Sergio Gor on the Sidelines of the BRICS Summit
dek: Cooperation in artificial intelligence and digitalization was discussed at the Sept. 12 meeting in New Delhi. Gor conveyed Donald Trump's personal congratulations; Tokayev reiterated his invitation for Trump to visit Kazakhstan.

title: Elena Rybakina Beats Sabalenka in the US Open Final and Becomes World No. 1
dek: The Kazakh player won 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 in the final in New York on Sept. 12. It is her third Grand Slam title.

title: PISA 2025 Results: Uzbekistan Leads the Region in Science, Kazakhstan's Math Score Declines
dek: In the OECD study, Uzbekistan posted the highest result in Central Asia with 438 points, a gain of 83 points over 2022 — the largest jump among all participants.

title: Mirziyoyev and Pashinyan Hold Phone Call: Trade Up 2.1-Fold Over Seven Months
dek: The Sept. 11 conversation covered industrial cooperation and the unblocking of regional communications.

title: 25 Years Since 9/11: The New York Ceremony and the Debate Over Muslim Americans
dek: Four former presidents attended the memorial service at Ground Zero. The presence of Zohran Mamdani, the city's first Muslim mayor, drew debate of its own.

title: A $350 Million Fuel Processing Complex Is Being Built in the Talas Region
dek: On Sept. 11, Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and the Kazakh company QAZAQ BITUM Processing signed a memorandum of intent.

title: Two Men Given Two Aggravated Life Sentences Each for Killing Two Uzbek Women in Istanbul
dek: The Istanbul Anadolu 17th High Criminal Court found Dilshod Turdimurotov and Gofurjon Kamolkhojayev guilty of murdering Durdona Hakimova and Sayyora Ergashaliyeva. The case began in January with a body found in a dumpster in the Şişli district.

title: Uzbekistan–Japan Economic Committees Meet in Tashkent: A Portfolio of 75 Projects Worth $12 Billion
dek: More than 130 Japanese participants attended the 18th meeting. The priority areas are energy, chemicals, machine building, critical minerals, health care and IT.

title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Appointed Manager of the Tashkent International Financial Centre
dek: Under a presidential decree, the head of the Presidential Administration will perform the new role concurrently. The center operates under a separate regime based on English law and is scheduled to launch in 2027.

title: Senate Approves New Version of the Uzbek Alphabet: 28 Letters and One Apostrophe
dek: On Sept. 10, the Senate of the Oliy Majlis approved a law replacing the letters Sh, Ch, O‘ and G‘ with Ş, Ç, Ö and Ğ. If the law takes effect, first-grade textbooks will switch in 2027, with the full transition completed by 2031.

title: Dispute Over Iran Sanctions at the UN Security Council: An 11-to-2 Vote
dek: The Council discussed the work of the 1737 Committee on Sept. 10. Russia and China voted against the agenda. On Sept. 8, Britain introduced legislation imposing new sectoral restrictions on Iran.

title: The Sary-Tash Logistics Center Near the Chinese Border: Up to $100 Million in Investment Planned
dek: Kyrgyzstan's National Investment Agency signed a memorandum on Sept. 10. The route covers the China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan–Afghanistan corridor, with later access to Pakistan.

title: Summer 2026 Was the Second-Hottest in Uzbekistan's History
dek: According to Uzhydromet, seasonal temperatures ran 1.2 to 2.6 degrees above normal. Some areas recorded their hottest summer on observational record; August was record-hot across much of the country.

title: Freight Along the Middle Corridor Rose 22 Percent, but Eastbound Cargo Lags
dek: In January–August 2026, the westbound direction accounted for 80 percent of container flows on the Trans-Caspian route. Only 20 percent moved east.

title: “Space Days Kazakhstan 2026”: A Nine-Satellite International Constellation and Plans Beyond Baikonur
dek: At the forum held Sept. 7–9 in Astana and Baikonur, Kazakhstan presented a plan to assemble a constellation of Earth observation satellites by 2030.

title: The 126-Megawatt Sarimay Solar Plant in Khorezm Comes Fully Online
dek: 184,328 panels have been installed at the plant; annual output is roughly 252 gigawatt-hours. Uzbekistan plans to add 6.7 GW of new capacity by the end of 2026.

title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Grew 11.1 Percent in Seven Months, With Inflation Above 11 Percent
dek: The growth rate remains the highest in the region. According to the National Bank, annual inflation stood at 11.7 percent as of Aug. 24.

title: Astana Finance Days: Debating How to Reduce Kazakhstan's Reliance on Banks
dek: At the forum held on the AIFC platform on Sept. 9, senior financiers pointed to the need to deepen the capital market.

title: $8 Billion in State Assets Put Up for Sale: Turonbank, IBC and Uzexpocentre on the List
dek: Under a presidential decree signed Aug. 28, state stakes in 62 companies will be put up for auction by 2028. Proceeds of 14 trillion soums are planned by year's end; a “golden share” mechanism will be introduced at strategic enterprises.

title: The Hijab Debate in Kazakhstan: Private Schools Could Lose Their Licenses
dek: On Sept. 8, Education Minister Zhuldyz Suleimenova said private schools that permit the hijab could lose their licenses. The muftiate proposed finding a legal mechanism; the debate spread widely on social media.

title: Uzbekistan and Serbia Establish a Strategic Partnership: 20 Documents Signed in Belgrade
dek: A joint declaration was signed at the close of Mirziyoyev's first visit to Belgrade. The two sides agreed to open negotiations on a free trade agreement, launch direct Belgrade–Tashkent flights and support the Middle Corridor.

title: Israeli Ministers Unveil Plans to Displace Gaza's Population; U.S. Rejects Forced Displacement
dek: National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir presented a seven-year plan called “Separation 710.” Defense Minister Israel Katz called displacement “the only solution.” The U.S. State Department rejected forced displacement.

title: Mass Attack on Kyiv: 5 Killed, 142 Drones and 31 Missiles Shot Down
dek: The Sept. 8 attack on Ukraine's capital came after the end of a three-day pause that followed visits by U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. According to Klitschko, 30 people were wounded.

title: HUMO Stablecoin Pilot Begins in Uzbekistan: Token Pegged 1:1 to the Soum to Be Tested at More Than 20 Retail Locations
dek: The National Agency of Perspective Projects has registered Humo Digital. The token is backed by government securities, and the trial will run for 12 months.

title: Uzbekistan Appoints Its First-Ever Ambassador to Syria
dek: Ayubkhon Yunusov presented copies of his credentials to Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani. The two sides discussed creating an intergovernmental commission on trade and economic cooperation and a mechanism for political consultations.

title: “China Conference: Central Asia 2026” in Astana: China–Region Trade Passes $100 Billion
dek: The forum held on the AIFC platform on Sept. 7 was organized in Central Asia for the first time by a Hong Kong publication. The themes were capital, resources and the digital Silk Road.

title: Nomad Games Conclude: Popularity Exposed Organizational Shortcomings
dek: Problems with transport, sanitation and ticketing were recorded at the 6th World Nomad Games, which closed Sept. 6. Of 7,000 tickets sold for the kokpar final, 2,500 were found to be invalid.

title: World Nomad Games Conclude: 113 Countries, 3,000 Athletes, Kazakhstan Leads the Medal Count
dek: The sixth World Nomad Games ran from Aug. 31 to Sept. 6 in Kyrgyzstan and were the largest edition in the competition's history. The opening was held in Bishkek and the closing ceremony in Cholpon-Ata.

title: Witkoff and Kushner Hold Three Hours of Talks With Putin in Moscow
dek: The U.S. special envoys discussed Trump's proposal on Sept. 5. No official breakthrough was announced after the meeting; the Kremlin called the conversation “constructive.”

title: Tensions Around the Strait of Hormuz: U.S. Destroys Three Tankers, Iran Promises a “Harsher Response”
dek: On Sept. 5, U.S. forces struck oil tankers linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guard. Tehran warned it would step up attacks on U.S. warships.

title: Uzbekistan Developing an “Adaptive Social Protection” Strategy With the World Bank and UNICEF
dek: A discussion held Sept. 4 examined mechanisms for rapidly supporting families hit by climate, natural and economic shocks.

title: Kyrgyzstan Announces an $850 Million Climate Adaptation Plan
dek: The national plan, running through 2035, has been put up for public discussion. According to the document, the country's glacier area has shrunk 16 to 17 percent since the start of the 21st century, and the rivers' peak flow period has shifted 50 days earlier.

title: The Iran War Reignites in September: U.S. Strikes and Attacks on Bases in Kuwait and the UAE
dek: The U.S. carried out new strikes on Iranian territory on Sept. 1; four people were killed at a wedding in Sirik, Hormozgan. On Sept. 3, the Iranian army attacked military bases in Kuwait and the UAE. The SCO summit condemned the strikes.

title: Uzbekistan's Economy Over Seven Months: Retail Trade Up 20.2 Percent, Market Services Up 16.7 Percent
dek: According to statistical data, consumer demand and the services sector were the main sources of growth. The number of operating enterprises passed 509,800.

title: Direct Almaty–Urgench Flights Launch, Shortening the Trip to Khiva
dek: FlyArystan has been flying the route twice a week since Sept. 3. Flight time is 2 hours 35 minutes.

title: Construction Begins on Central Asia's Tallest Building in Dushanbe: 340 Meters, 77 Floors
dek: Emomali Rahmon laid the foundation stone for the Dushanbe Tower complex on Sept. 3. The project covers 29 hectares and is scheduled for completion in five years.

title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Move From Trade to Production Chains: $2.8 Billion in Half a Year
dek: Kazakhstan is Uzbekistan's third-largest trading partner. The two countries are carrying out 80 joint projects worth $1.8 billion.

title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan Sign 17 Documents in Bishkek, Targeting $200 Million in Trade
dek: A transit trade agreement, an extradition treaty and a series of memorandums were signed during Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's visit. Bilateral trade currently stands at around $16 million.

title: Raid in Gaza City: At Least Four Palestinians Killed in the Attacks
dek: On Sept. 1, Israeli forces carried out an operation to detain the head of Hamas's internal security service. Two children were reported killed in strikes launched to cover the withdrawal.

title: Migration Controls Widen in Moscow From Sept. 1: The “Amina” Requirement Now Applies to Non-Working Foreigners
dek: The pilot regime has been extended to citizens of visa-free countries staying more than 90 days in Moscow and the surrounding region, including students. Entries from Central Asia for work fell 15 percent in half a year.

title: The SCO Summit in Bishkek: 28 Documents Signed, Strikes on Iran Condemned
dek: The summit marking the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's 25th anniversary was held in Bishkek on Aug. 31–Sept. 1. The final declaration assessed the military strikes on Iranian territory as a violation of international law, and the chairmanship passed to Pakistan.

title: Mirziyoyev Proposes an “SCO-2040: Common Space of Development” Concept
dek: At the Bishkek summit, Uzbekistan's president called for making the SCO Development Bank operational, creating an Industrial Cooperation Map, building an open multilingual data corpus and restoring regular dialogue with Afghanistan.
